correctness.rationale: Directly reconstructed domination in L(K_n) as (at most one isolated ground vertex; no isolated-edge selected component). Any cyclic component admits redundant edge deletion. In a spanning minimal forest, leaf deletion forces every component to be P3. With an isolated ground vertex, every internal edge must split off an isolated edge, yielding exactly trees of diameter <=4 with arms of one or two edges; the P4 two-center overcount in the labeled EGF is corrected by x^4 z^3/2. Edge-count bounds and n=3,4,5 residue cases follow. Independent exhaustive actual open-neighborhood enumeration of every candidate for n=3..7 reproduced {3:3z^2,4:12z^2,5:80z^3,6:840z^4,7:630z^4+3402z^5}. The arbitrary-n proof is structural, not this finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Every inclusion-minimal total dominating set of the classical triangular graph is characterized and counted by size, determining upper total domination and the nonuniform distribution. The full infinite-family component classification is a natural structural invariant, rather than a restatement of the already known minimum.

final_claim: For each n>=3, inclusion-minimal total dominating sets of J(n,2)=L(K_n) correspond exactly to spanning disjoint P3 components or one isolated ground vertex with all remaining components short-legged spiders. The complete cardinality EGF is n![x^n](exp(x^3 z^2/2)+x exp(H)), with H=x(exp(xz+x^2 z^2)-1-xz-x^2 z^2)-x^4 z^3/2; upper total domination is max(2,n-2). The scalar minimum gamma_t=ceil(2(n-1)/3) is prior literature.
